findings.detail: Shortening destroyed the sense. kaikki's sense 0 is "to risk, to not spare, to make (every effort), to use"; stripping the parenthetical left "make" and "use" as bare verbs, and "not spare" as a fragment. The result reads as four unrelated generic verbs rather than a meaning. The verb lives almost entirely in the collocation "alles daransetzen" / "seine ganze Kraft daransetzen": to stake something on an aim, to devote all one's effort to it.

Ungrammatical English produced by dropping a parenthetical. kaikki sense 0 is "to add (on top) of something"; deleting "(on top)" leaves "add of something", which is not a usable phrase. The verb means to add something on top of what is already there (etwas draufgeben).

The literal sense was shipped over the ones the verb actually carries in use. Plain "carry away" is expressed by wegtragen; davontragen is nearly always figurative — Verletzungen/einen Schaden davontragen (sustain an injury), den Sieg/den Preis davontragen (carry off the victory). Those are candidate_glosses indices 1 ("to achieve, obtain") and 2 ("to suffer").

"arrive" collides with ankommen and does not name what dazukommen does. The verb means to join something already in progress or, very commonly, to be added on top of what precedes — "dazu kommt, dass …" (on top of that …). candidate_glosses index 1 is "to be added"; the joining sense is what a learner meets first.

"die" is the gloss for plain sterben and drops everything the dahin- prefix contributes. Like dahinsiechen and dahinvegetieren, this verb names a gradual dying — wasting away over time, or a population dying off one after another — not the event of death.

"be sick" is faithful to candidate_glosses index 0 but misleads twice: in British English "be sick" reads as "vomit", and the elevated German verb applies well beyond illness — die Wirtschaft / der Handel liegt darnieder. The sense is lying prostrate, laid low, in a slump; index 1 ("to languish") is closer.
